propositions: The review-bot uvicorn access log records the full request line including query string, causing the webhook token parameter (?token=...) to be written in plaintext to stderr and journald on every /webhook and /rerun request.

The WEBHOOK_TOKEN and /rerun token are both derived from GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN, making the plaintext token a valid Gerrit credential accessible to anyone reading the container journal, log excerpts, or any future log-shipping system.
The credential exposure is fail-open with no error signal, so the secret leaks continuously without alerting operators until discovered through manual log inspection.
Moving the authentication token from query parameter to X-Rebar-Token HTTP header, which uvicorn access logs do not record, prevents the secret from appearing in the request line.
A TokenRedactingFilter on the uvicorn.access logger provides a backstop to scrub token= patterns from logs while preserving route and status information for observability.
The previously-logged token must be rotated independently after the code fix lands, since the exposure already exists in journald and shared log excerpts.
